# Latex Fit Lab — full reference

Source: https://latex-tools.pages.dev — Last updated 2026-09-29.

## Why a latex garment is cut smaller than you are
Latex sheeting is elastic: it is not cut to the body measurement but to a smaller one, so that the
sheet is stretched while worn. The amount it is cut smaller is the reduction. Thin sheet stretches
more, so it takes a larger reduction; thick sheet stretches less, so it takes a smaller one.

## Reduction by thickness (base values, circumference)
- 0.25 mm (ultra thin): 14-17%
- 0.40 mm (standard): 12-15%
- 0.60 mm (heavy): 10-13%
- 0.80 mm (rigid): 8-11%
- 1.00 mm (extra rigid): 6-9%

## Per-part adjustment (percentage points added to the base reduction)
thigh +2, upper arm +2, waist +1, chest 0, hip 0, underbust −1, neck −5.
A positive number means the part is cut tighter than the base value, a negative number means looser.
Torso length is treated separately: cut 2-4% shorter, not by the circumference rule.

## Fit preference
relaxed −2 points, standard 0, snug +2 points, applied to every value.

## The nine measurements
Chest/bust, underbust, waist, hip, thigh, upper arm, neck, torso length, and the height/size used to
match the sheet. Take them with a soft tailor's tape.

## The three measurements that go wrong most
- Torso length: run the tape straight down from the side of the neck, over the bust, to the crotch. Following the body curve makes it short, and a catsuit that is short in the torso cannot be corrected later.
- Thigh: at the widest point, immediately below the crotch, not further down the leg.
- Upper arm: arm hanging relaxed at the side, not flexed and not pressed against the chest.

## Questions people ask
Q: What size latex catsuit should I order?
A: Latex sizes are not standardised. Send the nine measurements or the finished-measurement sheet instead of a size letter.

Q: Does thinner latex need to be cut smaller?
A: Yes. 0.25 mm takes a 14-17% reduction; 1.00 mm takes 6-9%.

Q: Is the reduction the same everywhere on the body?
A: No. Thigh and upper arm are cut tighter than the base, the neck is cut looser.
